findings.title: deleteMany OR condition missing method filter will delete non-SMS reminders
findings.body: The second branch of the OR in deleteMany (`{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }`) does not include a `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` filter. This means any WorkflowReminder row (including EMAIL and WHATSAPP methods) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted. While currently only this SMS code path increments retryCount, the query is semantically incorrect and will silently delete reminders of other methods if retryCount is ever used elsewhere or if data is manually modified. The fix is to add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` to the second OR condition.

findings.title: Database update inside catch block can throw and crash the handler
findings.body: If the `prisma.workflowReminder.update` inside the catch block (line 190) itself throws (e.g., the reminder was already deleted by the deleteMany at the top of the handler, or a transient DB error), the exception will propagate unhandled out of the for-loop, aborting processing of all remaining reminders. This inner database call should be wrapped in its own try-catch to ensure one failed update does not prevent other reminders from being processed.

findings.title: Stale retryCount value used for increment may lose updates under concurrent execution
findings.body: The update uses `reminder.retryCount + 1` based on the value read at the start of the loop iteration. If the cron job is invoked concurrently (e.g., overlapping cron schedules or retries), two executions could read the same retryCount and both write retryCount+1, effectively losing one increment. Using Prisma's atomic increment (`retryCount: { increment: 1 }`) would be safer and also more idiomatic.
